details: DocumentRequest.oneOf references ContentString and ContentUri, but neither branch requires its property and both allow additional properties. Every provider-published content-only example therefore validates against both branches and fails oneOf. The node sends the documented content request shapes; adding an invalid contentUri merely to distinguish the schemas would contradict those examples. Request fixtures retain the published examples verbatim.

The /semantics/similar JSON String and Options examples supply options.resultLanguages as ["eng", "spa", "deu", "jpn"], but SimilarTermsOptions.items references LanguageCode objects. The node uses the documented string-code list.

The /address-similarity JSON String example supplies address2 as a free-form string, but Address.oneOf permits only AddressFielded or AddressString objects. Ordinary valid fielded/address objects also match both optional-property object branches. The node supports documented free-form address strings and does not invent fields to evade oneOf.
